nodes.label: AccessContext.jurisdiction_team_ids
nodes.rationale: RBAC-5J addition: structurally independent tuple of team ids over which an OrgRole.MANAGER holds supervisory jurisdiction, distinct from team_ids (membership).

nodes.label: TEAM-jurisdiction authorization branch (RBAC-5J)
nodes.rationale: Only built when access.role == OrgRole.MANAGER and access.jurisdiction_team_ids is non-empty; structurally independent of the membership branch — a jurisdiction team id never needs to also be a membership team id.

nodes.label: DocumentService._can_create
nodes.rationale: Authorizes the requested document access scope before any file is validated or stored; TEAM creation is a membership check (any OrgRole/TeamRole qualifies), ORGANISATION requires OrgRole.ADMIN, and organisation_id is always sourced from AccessContext, never the client.

nodes.label: OrgManagerTeamService
nodes.rationale: Only OrgRole.ADMIN may grant or revoke jurisdiction; authorization runs before any database read, then team/target-user are resolved in the ADMIN's own organisation, then the target's current OrgRole is verified to be MANAGER before granting.

nodes.label: TeamMembershipService
nodes.rationale: Distinct from TeamService because it uses a different authorization model (per-team TeamRole rather than org-wide OrgRole); implements exactly four operations gated on that specific team's own TeamRole.MANAGER.

nodes.label: Last-manager invariant (DELETE-embedded correlated subquery)
nodes.rationale: Enforced by the DELETE statement itself (correlated subquery in WHERE), not a prior SELECT count, to close a genuine race where two concurrent removals of two different managers on a two-manager team could both succeed and leave zero managers.

nodes.label: TEAM-ADMIN authorization branch (RBAC-5J)
nodes.rationale: A deliberate behavior change: OrgRole.ADMIN gained unconditional TEAM-document read visibility across their own organisation, regardless of membership or jurisdiction, superseding ADMIN's previous membership-only TEAM visibility.

nodes.label: Conversation memory (rolling summary + recent window)
nodes.rationale: Long conversations do not send the whole transcript to the answer LLM; a rolling summary plus recent window keeps prompt size flat as the conversation grows while still catching up after a failed refresh.

nodes.label: Developed India 2020
nodes.rationale: Vision organized around empowering villages, rural core competence, connectivity and a youth movement toward development.

nodes.label: Multi-head attention
nodes.rationale: Parallel attention heads over projected subspaces widen what the model can attend to at once.

nodes.label: Scaled dot-product attention
nodes.rationale: Dot-product attention scaled by 1/sqrt(d_k) for stable gradients.

nodes.label: Positional encoding
nodes.rationale: Parameter-free sinusoidal signal supplies token order to an order-agnostic attention stack.

nodes.label: Self-attention
nodes.rationale: Relates all positions of a sequence to compute its representation with constant sequential cost.

nodes.label: Transformer architecture
nodes.rationale: A simple encoder-decoder built solely on attention, replacing recurrence/convolution for parallelism and lower training cost.

nodes.label: Deep bidirectional pre-training
nodes.rationale: Standard left-to-right LMs restrict architecture choice; joint left/right conditioning in all layers unlocks stronger representations.

nodes.label: Fine-tuning for downstream tasks
nodes.rationale: One extra output layer plus fine-tuning all parameters avoids task-specific architecture engineering.

nodes.label: Masked language model (MLM)
nodes.rationale: Randomly mask tokens and predict them so a deep model can condition on both left and right context without seeing itself.

nodes.label: Next sentence prediction (NSP)
nodes.rationale: Pre-train sentence-pair relationships to help tasks like QA and NLI that hinge on inter-sentence reasoning.

nodes.label: Transformer foundation of LLMs
nodes.rationale: Survey traces LLM progress to the transformer architecture, compute scaling and large training corpora.

nodes.label: Advanced RAG
nodes.rationale: Add pre- and post-retrieval optimization to fix Naive RAG's retrieval-quality and integration problems.

nodes.label: Modular RAG
nodes.rationale: Decompose RAG into reconfigurable modules for flexibility beyond a fixed retrieve-then-read chain.

nodes.label: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
nodes.rationale: Retrieve relevant chunks from an external knowledge base to curb hallucination, stale knowledge and opaque reasoning in LLMs.
